metadata.title: DeeJay Dallas a Deep-League Handcuff to Add in Week 4
metadata.description: Minnesota Vikings running back DeeJay Dallas has some fantasy appeal in deeper leagues ahead of Week 4. Dallas is firmly entrenched in the No. 2 role behind Aaron Jones Sr. (knee), but therein lies a potential opportunity for the veteran ball-carrier to take on a bigger workload. Jones has struggled to stay fully healthy in the back half of his career, and Dallas would likely see the biggest bump in volume if Jones were to miss any time due to injury. Although he wouldn't have the backfield all to himself because Demond Claiborne would also rotate in, Dallas would be the biggest riser in this hypothetical scenario where Jones gets hurt while Jordan Mason (thumb) is still on injured reserve. Because of Dallas' handcuff status, the 28-year-old has some waiver wire appeal in very deep fantasy leagues ahead of Week 4.

metadata.title: DeeJay Dallas (toe) will play Sunday
metadata.description: DeeJay Dallas (toe) will play in Sunday's game against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers.
metadata.analysis: Dallas is going to be available to play on Sunday, as his toe injury is not considered a substantial issue for him right now. Aaron Jones Sr. (knee) has also been cleared to play, however, which will render Dallas irrelevant from a fantasy perspective this week.

metadata.title: DeeJay Dallas - Clear for Week 3
metadata.description: Dallas (toe) practiced fully Friday and doesn't have a designation for Sunday's game in Tampa Bay.
metadata.analysis: Dallas kicked off Week 3 prep with back-to-back limited sessions due to a toe injury, but his ability to handle every on-field rep Friday clears him to be available to the Vikings backfield this weekend. With Aaron Jones (knee) also gaining clearance to play Sunday, Dallas likely will remain relegated to a small workload, as the latter has just four touches on his 14 offensive snaps through two games on the campaign.

metadata.title: DeeJay Dallas (toe) limited Thursday
metadata.description: DeeJay Dallas (toe) was limited at practice on Thursday.
metadata.analysis: Dallas was unable to practice in full on Thursday and remained limited due to his toe injury. He seems likely to play this week still, but fantasy managers shouldn't expect him to play more than a depth role this week with Aaron Jones Sr. (knee) trending towards playing against the Buccaneers.

metadata.title: DeeJay Dallas - Turns in limited practice
metadata.description: Dallas (toe) was a limited participant in Thursday's practice.
metadata.analysis: When Minnesota has all of its key backfield options available, Dallas is expected to play exclusively on special teams, but he'll likely be needed to serve as a passing-down or change-of-pace option at the very least during Sunday's game at Tampa Bay, provided the toe issue doesn't keep him from playing. Jordan Mason (thumb) won't be eligible to return from injured reserve until Week 7, and Aaron Jones -- who handled 23 touches and an 81 percent snap share in the Week 2 win over the Bears -- joined Dallas as a limited participant in Thursday's practice. If Jones ends up sitting out Sunday or has his snaps managed more carefully, Dallas could be in store for a more prominent role after he was limited to eight offensive snaps and three touches in Week 2.

metadata.title: DeeJay Dallas - Limited practice Wednesday
metadata.description: Dallas (toe) was a limited participant at the Vikings' practice Wednesday.
metadata.analysis: Dallas appears to have picked up a toe injury during the team's 9-3 win over the Bears in Week 2, and as a result, he wasn't able to practice in full to open the week. With Aaron Jones (knee) listed as a non-participant Wednesday, rookie running back Demond Claiborne is the only fully healthy option at the moment. Dallas will have two more chances to log a full practice before Sunday's matchup with the Buccaneers.

metadata.title: DeeJay Dallas (toe) listed as limited Wednesday
metadata.description: DeeJay Dallas (toe) was listed as a limited participant at practice on Wednesday.
metadata.analysis: Dallas was not able to practice in full on Wednesday due to a toe injury that he's dealing with. Aaron Jones (knee) is at risk of being sidelined in Week 3, in which case the 28-year old would be primed for more work than usual against the Buccaneers, assuming he himself is healthy.

metadata.title: DeeJay Dallas Can Stay on the Waiver Wire
metadata.description: Minnesota Vikings running back DeeJay Dallas got three touches in Week 2, but there still is not much of a fantasy case here. He carried twice for eight yards and caught one pass for 12 yards against Chicago after making a one-yard catch in the opener. Jordan Mason's fractured thumb and move to injured reserve opened a roster spot for Dallas, not a meaningful role. Minnesota still lists Aaron Jones Sr. first on the depth chart, Demond Claiborne second and Dallas third. Jones handled 23 carries in Week 2, while Claiborne remains the more interesting stash if managers want exposure to this backfield. RotoBaller's September 23 mid-week waiver rankings have Claiborne 55th overall and leave Dallas off the top 85 entirely. That lines up with the usage. Dallas can stay on waivers in standard leagues and does not need to be rostered unless the Vikings lose another back.

metadata.title: DeeJay Dallas - Catches sole target in tight win
metadata.description: Dallas rushed twice for eight yards and caught his sole target for 12 yards in Sunday's 9-3 win over the Bears.
metadata.analysis: Dallas played eight offensive snaps, totaling 20 yards in a game where offense was rare. The running back also contributed eight special-teams reps, filling in wherever he could while starting rusher Aaron Jones  took most of the carries.

metadata.title: DeeJay Dallas sees three touches in Week 2
metadata.description: DeeJay Dallas rushed twice for eight yards while also catching his only target for 12 yards in the Vikings' 9-3 win over the Chicago Bears in Week 2.
metadata.analysis: Dallas remains more of an afterthought in the Minnesota offense early on, recording three touches or less in each of the first two games. The running back can be left off rosters with Aaron Jones Sr. commanding the majority of the backfield work, with a Week 3 contest against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers up next.

metadata.title: DeeJay Dallas - Signed to Vikings' active roster
metadata.description: The Vikings signed Dallas from the practice squad to the active roster Wednesday.
metadata.analysis: With Jordan Mason (thumb) landing on injured reserve, Dallas will presumably jump into a prominent role behind Aaron Jones. The 2020 No. 144 overall pick has appeared in contests for the Seahawks, Cardinals, Panthers, Jaguars and Vikings during his career. In 84 regular-season games, Dallas accumulated 538 yards and four touchdowns off 124 carries, adding 64 catches for 407 yards and two touchdowns.

metadata.title: DeeJay Dallas signs with Vikings' active roster
metadata.description: DeeJay Dallas is signing a deal to join Minnesota's 53-man active roster.
metadata.analysis: Minnesota is giving Dallas a spot on their active roster after placing Jordan Mason (thumb) on injured reserve, which will knock him out for at least four weeks. Dallas isn't expected to play more than a depth role on this offense, however, with Aaron Jones Sr. primed to step up and take on the role as the primary back on this offense for the foreseeable future.

metadata.title: DeeJay Dallas - Reverts to Minnesota's practice squad
metadata.description: Dallas reverted to the Vikings' practice squad Monday, per the NFL's transaction log.
metadata.analysis: Dallas played just six offensive snaps in Sunday's win over the Packers. The running back made a larger impact on special teams, logging one tackle on kick coverage over 14 special teams snaps. Dallas can only be elevated two more times, and after that may only play for the Vikings if he is signed to the active roster.

metadata.title: DeeJay Dallas - Elevated for Sunday
metadata.description: The Vikings elevated Dallas from the practice squad to the active roster Saturday, Craig Peters of the team's official site reports.
metadata.analysis: Dallas signed with the Vikings on Sept. 2 after being released by the Jaguars during cutdown day. The running back will likely provide a special teams presence in Sunday's game against the Packers with minimal offensive usage.

metadata.title: DeeJay Dallas signs with Vikings
metadata.description: The Vikings signed RB DeeJay Dallas to their practice squad.
metadata.analysis: Dallas will add depth in the backfield for Minnesota.
